quest.title: The Solution of Fate
quest.description: Following the clues from the previous chapter, you head to Dragonspine to find Albedo. It seems the mysteries around Durin are about to be revealed, but the trials prepared by "fate" are waiting for you as well...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x600, Primogem x60, Mora x62225, Guide to Ballad x5, Tale of "Durin" x1, Hero's Wit x7, Mystic Enhancement Ore x14

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: So this is the other Durin, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: If this had been the dragon that ended up being revived in Mondstadt, there's no telling what kind of calamity the people would have had to endure.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: So, if you think about it like that, Durin's actually a hero.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: And, you just thought you'd be nice all of a sudden?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: No, I'm just a little envious, that's all. Not everyone gets a chance to be a hero.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Actually, most of the credit belongs to Albedo...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Then again, barely anyone even remembers you at this point, so I guess there's not much left to envy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You... Ugh.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Ah, so you three still remember Durin. Looks like the memory loss hasn't spread to close friends... yet.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I guess that means my memory of you must still be complete as well.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Albedo...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're finally here! Boy, do we have a whole pile of questions for you...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Ah, you're here too.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I think I've pieced together some of what happened to him. But what's your take on things?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Master Jean filled me in on what happened, and I've got a few theories, but let's get on the same page first.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You exchange intel with Albedo, who also checks how Durin is holding up.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Well, physically he's doing fine. His body is holding the Abyssal power at bay, and there's nothing whatsoever to indicate any risk of collapse.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, from an alchemy point of view, there's nothing wrong with him?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The issue isn't so much that the Abyssal power within him has gotten out of control. It's that the connection between his will and body is fading.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: If he ends up losing his conscious will, his body will fall back on its biological instincts — and that's when the Abyssal power within it will take over.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But if that happens...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: This book mentioned a witches' gathering. It seems like quite a few of these "witches" got themselves involved in Durin's case, which brings me to my theory.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Bringing fairytale Durin into this world to replace the Durin on Dragonspine means using one Durin's fate to overwrite the other's.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: But, the power of alchemy alone would not be enough to pull off such a feat...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It would have required the combined use of Miss Barbeloth's astrology, my teacher's alchemy, and Aunt Alice's magic.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: After learning of Miss Barbeloth's prophecy, Durin and I finally came up with a way to settle the Dragonspine-Durin problem for good.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: And I took care of the alchemy side of things, which, looking back on it, seems to have been a part of their plan all along.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: So now, there's only one thing missing...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The "magic," right?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: As for the "fate" theory our friend in the hat just mentioned...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I still can't figure out how any kind of magic could possibly influence the fate of Teyvat, but I'm certain that the answer lies within this book.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So the reason Alice had us complete this book... was to make that magic possible?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: A form of magic powerful enough to rewrite fate itself...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Well, we've no time to lose. I just need to take a look at the book.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: The next part of the story most likely relates to me, so the memory that unlocks it must be connected to me too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Unknown Voice
dialogues.text: The giant tree was home to a broken branch, the shape of its splintered arm aligning perfectly with the branch that had burst forth from the castle walls.

dialogues.speaker: Unknown Voice
dialogues.text: Join yourself to that broken bough, for there you may take root at last — and henceforth bask in the sun and rain of the world beyond the castle.

dialogues.speaker: Unknown Voice
dialogues.text: But first, fetch the stickiest clay, and let it bind the scar of the break.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: I see...

talks.objective: Enter the world within the book

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ready when you are.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is this place?
It looks like it's modeled after an alchemist's workshop — or rather, a cliched stereotype of one...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...Albedo?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Hold on, why do I look like this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh yeah, we forgot to tell you... Basically, the characters in the story are reflections of how Durin sees them.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: At least you're still human-shaped.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Since "Cat Guy" has taken on a different appearance too, that must mean the two of us are both "characters" in this story.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: But you, Paimon, and Durin haven't changed at all. Hm, you must be special figures in some way...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Ugh, I'd like to know more about that too, but seeing as none of them can explain it, let's just concentrate on moving the plot forward.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's take a look around.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is that... a hidden path?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: And just like that, the group stumbled upon a hidden passageway. Intricately crafted, it seemed to lead them towards another exciting chapter of the tale...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, what are we waiting for? Next chapter, here we c— Ouch!

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: But this was a chapter that had not yet been written. Ahead of them was a storyless void, and they could go no further.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Then what's the point of having a path here?

choices.text: Maybe the author had a flash of inspiration...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like a pretty bad habit for a writer!

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Hm? Over here. I found something.

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: What the clay figure found was none other than the evil dragon's heart itself. Though the creature had perished long ago, its heart was still there, pulsing away and growing warmer with every beat.

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: And the clay alchemist knew what it meant — that the evil dragon would return one day, just as the prophecy had foretold.

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: Yet guided by his mother's wisdom, he foresaw another fate. If only the alchemist could bestow this heart upon the little dragon, he might be reborn in the evil dragon's stead.

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: Only then would the evil dragon's heart grow still, and the little one inherit its tale.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Sounds like this chapter's about Albedo bringing me to life?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: If that really was the solution, though, this would have been over the minute I finished the transmutation. So why is Durin still being forgotten?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: There has to be some other reason.

choices.text: There are still places we can check.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Yeah, I'd like to explore the area a bit more.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The evil dragon's heart continued to beat, as if waiting for the little dragon to accept it as his own.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Looks like we have no choice but to get this done.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Whatever happens next, Durin is going to need all of our help. Is everyone ready?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Returning to the castle...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You seem like you're torn about something?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I just never thought crossing over into a new world would create so much trouble. All I wanted was to make some friends.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I'm starting to think I kinda miss being in Simulanka...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You might look back on it with fondness but, if I were you, I wouldn't miss it.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Why?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Sometimes, moving on with your life comes at a cost. But, that's better than going nowhere at all.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You don't have to worry, Durin. No matter what problem you face, there will always be a solution.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Okay...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: There you are...

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: Oh, hello there!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, it's Mini Durin again! What are you doing holed up in here?

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: I was worried I'd scare everyone off, so I've been hiding out here all this time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just like before.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: You must be really nervous, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: I... I guess I am a little nervous... But I'm also excited!

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: I'm gonna get to stop the evil dragon, and even become a "human"! It's all thanks to that clay man... He's the one who talked me into it!

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: And once I'm a human, I'll be able to make loads of friends and do tons of important things!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: You'll make lots of friends, that's for sure, and go on many unforgettable adventures...

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: I'm so glad to hear it! The only thing is, the clay man said becoming human isn't gonna be easy, so I'm feeling a little anxious too...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...He's right about that. Even if you manage to become a human, there will always be tougher challenges on the road ahead.

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: R—Really?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: But even so, your friends will be there to help you.

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: Oh? Then I'm not afraid!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Funny, isn't it? After talking to you, I'm not afraid anymore either.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: So, are you ready now?

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: Yep! I'm ready to become a human!

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The little dragon and his companions... blank... blank again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, what's going on? Are we running out of ink?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Once the ink runs out, is that the end of the story?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I had a feeling this would happen...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's happening to the others...?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Now that the story's ink was spent, all that lay ahead were blank pages.

talks.objective: The story will eventually reach its conclusion...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: As the little dragon slipped back inside the castle's walls, the clamor of the outside world fell away.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: There was no danger here, no problems for the little dragon to resolve.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: As soon as his mother finished her story, it was time for the child to drift off into the world of dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: And so the story ended — with the little dragon fast asleep in his castle, just like he had never even hatched.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: What's going on? I feel so weak...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what's happening? Durin, wake up!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We've reached an ending...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, but... this can't be how it ends! Durin promised to bring back everyone's memories... There's no way he'd accept an ending like this!

talks.objective: The prophecy is destined to come true...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: With the help of his friends, the little dragon destroyed the evil dragon's heart, using up every last ounce of his strength.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: In his eyes, this would ensure that his story, and his alone, remained in the world beyond the castle's walls.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: But the evil dragon's heart was like a great tree with roots digging deep beneath the surface. Cutting off the branches did not kill it. No, it just made it impossible for a new branch to take their place...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The gnarled roots retreated back into the frozen earth, biding their time for a chance to bud again. Cut off from their source, the rootless branches above the surface slowly withered away.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The little dragon's story faded into nothingness — and in the world beyond the castle, only the evil dragon's tale endured.

dialogues.speaker: Little Dragon
dialogues.text: Who... am I?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Is this... me?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: And so the story ended — with the little dragon fading from sight, leaving nothing but the evil dragon's shadow in his place.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, the story's over?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, but... that means Durin...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do we do now?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The little dragon and his companions... blank... blank again...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, what's going on? Are we running out of ink?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Once the ink runs out, is that the end of the story?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: I had a feeling this would happen...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's happening to the others...?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Now that the story's ink was spent, all that lay ahead were blank pages.

talks.objective: Discuss the current situation with everyone

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Finally, a happy ending! That must be the last step, right? Woohoo, we completed the story!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But, then why are we still here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Born anew, the little dragon set off once more, his story far from over.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So that wasn't the end?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: What comes next might be the most crucial part of all — the real "last step."

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Hmph. If fate really is as devious as they say, then I say... show us what you've got.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you're all so serious all of a sudden.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Urgh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Durin, are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The evil dragon's heart was now one with the little dragon, yet the dark power within it still lingered.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Would the little dragon dare to hold this power back, or would he simply... give in?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! What kind of question is that? Of course he's gonna control it. What choice does he have?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Time... is running out... So, would the little dragon dare to hold this power back, or would he simply... give in?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, what's up with the narrator...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (We've run out of ink... So much for Albedo's plan. We have to find another way.)

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Returning to the castle...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You seem like you're torn about something?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I just never thought crossing over into a new world would create so much trouble. All I wanted was to make some friends.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I'm starting to think I kinda miss being in Simulanka...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You might look back on it with fondness but, if I were you, I wouldn't miss it.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Why?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Sometimes, moving on with your life comes at a cost. But, that's better than going nowhere at all.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: You don't have to worry, Durin. No matter what problem you face, there will always be a solution.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Okay...

talks.objective: The story will eventually reach its conclusion...
The prophecy is destined to come true...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The little dragon was at an impasse, and the dark power within him surged like a tide.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Unchecked, the darkness engulfed everything around it, including the little dragon's soul.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: The little dragon's story faded into nothingness — and in the world beyond the castle, only the evil dragon's tale endured.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Is this... me?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: And so the story ended — with the little dragon fading from sight, leaving nothing but the evil dragon's shadow in his place.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, the story's over?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh no, but... that means Durin...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do we do now?

talks.objective: Discuss what to do with everyone

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's going on here? Why isn't the story letting Durin just suppress the Abyssal power? It keeps getting stuck...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Aghhh...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Hmm... It seems the act of suppressing the power counts as an "event" in the story. In other words, we would need ink to write it in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, what now? Did we use too much earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How are we supposed to write a happy ending with only this much left...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Hm... Well, this is Durin's story. As long as he's alive and well, why should it end?

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: If there really is such a direct correlation between the story and his fate, I may have a potential hypothesis.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Durin was — and still is, in essence — a storybook character written into being by "M." From the moment he was born, he has always dwelt within her story.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: ...And I suspect that has remained the case, even after his arrival in Teyvat.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Reviving Durin in the evil dragon's place was an act of grafting this Durin's "story" onto the latter's "fate." In essence, that is how his fate was rewritten.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: But there is a fundamental difference between a being's "story" and its "fate."

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: As Miss Barbeloth reminded us, the fate of every living being in Teyvat has been woven into the fabric of time. It's most natural path, therefore, is to proceed along its given track.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: But Durin's story, on the other hand...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: As Durin's connection to this world wore thin, not only have people started to forget him, he's started to lose control of the Abyssal power within.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: In other words, his story can't continue... because the author's ink is drying up. That's what it seems like to me.

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: It would seem the little dragon had made a group of fine friends indeed...

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Save it. The question is — are you here to help him, or stand in his way?

response.speaker: Narrator
response.text: This is as far... as the story can go... What path... will you choose?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: I suppose... the final decision is up to me.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: It's hard to believe I never actually left my mother's story. If that's true, I'd like to go there and see for myself.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: By "there," I take it you mean... the blank pages of the unwritten chapter ahead?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: B—But... we still don't even know how Alice's magic works.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If Durin belongs inside the story, then going outside of it, to some unwritten part... Isn't that too risky?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: ...I'm not afraid.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Then go for it. We'll be with you all the way.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: I second that. It would seem this is one answer you need to go seize for yourself.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: So be it. Whatever obstacles stand in your way, we'll tear them down together.

choices.text: It's just not time for the story to end.

talks.objective: Break through the boundary of the tale

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (So, we can't destroy the heart, and even if we tried, it would cause Durin to disappear. We have to find another way.)

talks.objective: Go to the blank pages beyond the story

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Gotta... keep going...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Ahead lies only... a storyless void...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: My consciousness... is slipping away...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Keep going, Durin. A pure soul is your essence, not an empty void.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I feel so... weak...

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Stand tall, Durin. You are not some amorphous idea. The body I made for you is flesh and bone.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Am I truly... alive?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Yes Durin, but you must keep going. You're as alive and real as I am.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Silence, huh... Have you nothing to say about my proposal?

dialogues.speaker: Rhinedottir
dialogues.text: Let me get this straight... You want to graft your story onto this unfinished thread of fate — and in doing so, not only rewrite that fate, but allow the story to live on...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Quite the brilliant idea. Still, the story's survival depends entirely on whether the author keeps writing...

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Exactly. And the moment foretold by the prophecy is still centuries away.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: ...I see.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: I thought my own ignorance might be the problem — that I'd asked more of the noble science of alchemy than it could ever deliver.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: ...Or, that I had failed to discern the heavenly signs and grasp the secret truth underlying the prophecy.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Little did I imagine that time itself would prove to be the greatest hurdle of all.

dialogues.speaker: Rhinedottir
dialogues.text: Well, my friend, this has been a most intriguing experiment. And from an academic perspective, at least, I don't think it was a bad proposal.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Someday, the prophecy will come to pass. So remember, my friend — much like the stars themselves, there will always be something that transcends the test of time.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Thank you, everyone... You've helped me so much already. But Alice, I still have one final favor to ask of you.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Will you lend me your magic one last time, just enough for me to keep his story alive until the prophecy is fulfilled?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: You mean, you want me to... hahaha, extend your lifespan?

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: No, not in that sense. As Rhinedottir once told me, the laws governing life and death are among the most unyielding in this world... I'm well aware of that.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Whether it lasts a day or an age, the span of one's life is determined by fate alone.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: If I tried to breach that law by force, I'm afraid I would lose what makes me human.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: This is not a path I want to go down. If I am to die, then I shall die a human.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: So... What is it that you want me to do?

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: I would like you to send this pen of mine into the future.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: ...I see. Then perhaps there really is a way I can help.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: I could create a kind of "story magic" to take over the writing once you're gone.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: But for it to work, you would need to provide enough of your own words for it to learn from.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: How much?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Oh, an immense amount... so much, in fact, that you would have to spend the rest of your life writing. And even then, I'm sorry to say, it would not last forever.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: No matter how much you write, there is a limit to the number of words you can leave behind, but the world itself will never stop changing.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Someday, perhaps, even your entire corpus will not be enough for the magic to continue describing this world. And when that happens, the story will end.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Still, it's worth a try.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: *coughing*...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Oh, my dear Anya. Even after all this time, you're still... *sigh* Look at you. You should be enjoying your old age in peace and quiet. Especially now that things are finally returning to normal after that terrible calamity...

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Once he leaves Simulanka, things will only get more complicated. If his story is to continue, there needs to be more material for the magic to draw upon... *coughs*

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: I'll just have to skip over some of the less important details... *coughing*

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Anya... Why do you insist on sending him out of the storybook world? Why must he face his fate in Teyvat?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Why not just let him remain within the story? With my magic, even fate's curse could be undone, and he could live happily ever after.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Mm, I suppose. In fairy tales, all it takes is a heartfelt wish, and even a wooden puppet can turn himself into a real boy... and live "happily ever after"...

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: That's just how fairy tales end, isn't it? But, have you ever wondered what happens to the main character after the "ever after"?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Hm...

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Tell me, Alice. In your eyes, what would be a writer's greatest regret?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: To... leave a story without an ending?

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Not a bad answer. It's true, many writers come to consider that their greatest regret. But I see things differently.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: My greatest regret is that every story I write has to come to an end in the first place.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Anya...

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: No matter how brilliantly a character shines, the moment their story ends, their potential is lost forever.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: For them, the story itself becomes an inescapable fate.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: But what if instead, I could place my pen in their hand and let them continue the story themselves?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: You mean...

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: You said it yourself, I can only leave so many words behind. Even with your magic, the idea that I could keep the story going until the prophecy comes to pass is wishful thinking at best.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: But I've found a way to use your magic to transform some of my finished stories into a special kind of ink.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: This ink is a magical medium he can use to complete the story the way he wants to.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: For what is storytelling, but another kind of magic? And if he can experience the whole tale himself while leaving behind his own wishes and aspirations...

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Even once he reaches the chapter where I stopped, he'll still be able to carry the story forward on his own.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: And so, by leaving him this ink, I can entrust him with the responsibility of writing his own story.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: A character with the power to write their own story...

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: That way, he'll finally be free from the cage that is my pen — and like anyone else living in the real world, he can go on to create a life of his own.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: And you no longer need to worry about the constraints of my magic... What a brilliant idea, Anya!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: B—But... there are still risks.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: First of all, once he arrives in Teyvat, he'll have to rely entirely on the story you left him to maintain his connection to that world.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: As you gradually hand over creative control, that connection will grow weaker, and at some point he might lose it altogether.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: But at the same time, he'll also have the chance to forge that connection for himself.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Mmm... The issue is, this method taps into too many of Teyvat's core secrets. Any overt hints you try to leave will be erased in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: In fact, it'd be hard for you to leave anything at all to guide them.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: We still have the story itself, though. I can use that to show them the way.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: It's entirely possible he burns through all your ink, never reaches the chapter you had in mind, and gets stuck roaming the chapters of his past.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: But despite all that, you...

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: ...I still believe in what this child can become.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: His hopes and wishes can be his "ink," so he won't be trapped by mine running dry.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Ah, what the writer you are, Anya. Your imagination never ceases to amaze.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: And, you do know how much I love a happy ending, hahahaha. You shall have my help, my dear.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Thank you, my friend.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Well then, my child. Do you understand what you must do?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Yes, I... think I do.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: It's my turn to keep this story alive.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Then what's holding you back?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...What will become of you after I take up this pen?

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: I will fade away. There will no longer be a reason for me to go on existing.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: My child, I... or your mother, I should say, passed away long ago. The voice you're hearing is nothing but a magical echo that has now fulfilled its purpose. You needn't feel so reluctant to let me go.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I know... I know my mother died long ago.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: It's just... when you lose your mom too soon, it's hard to tear yourself away from the stories she used to read. I guess it's a silly way of pretending she's still here, by your side...

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Durin...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: But after coming to this world and traveling it with my friends, facing all kinds of enemies together...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I suddenly realized, I couldn't just sit around listening to my mother's stories, because I'd found a new purpose in life.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Maybe this is just what growing up feels like. With all my new friends waiting, it's time I finally set aside my mother's storybook...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I'm ready to grow up now, Mom.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Mm... Then take this, a gift I should've given you a long time ago.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: You've witnessed this story from the very beginning... made your wishes, offered your blessings, and even wrote your choices into its pages.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: From here on out, this pen is yours.

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Now I ask of you, the other pillar of this story, as both its reader and its witness:

dialogues.speaker: Anya
dialogues.text: Will you turn the page so the next chapter can begin?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Turn the page...)

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Looks like this is the final step.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: A chance to strike back at fate? Now that's not something that comes knocking every day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Go get it, Durin!

dialogues.speaker: "Fate"
dialogues.text: I cannot die... I will be reborn... and bring calamity to all... It has been decreed... by fate itself!

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: No, that fate no longer defines me. In the end, only my story shall endure.

talks.objective: But His Story Is Far From Over

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Thank you, Mom...

talks.objective: But His Story Is Far From Over

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Is everyone okay?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're fine, thanks — and hey, we all saw how you fought back there. That was awesome!

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: I have to admit, I do feel like something in me has changed...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: I owe you all so much. Without your help, I don't know if I could have ever made it this far.

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Just a shame I could only help out from the sidelines. Like I said before, it's not every day that you get to put fate in its place...

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Mm... Well, I'm sure you'll hear it someday!

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: ...Hear what?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: The chance to strike back at fate knocking at your door!

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Heh... Yeah, maybe someday.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Allow me to just check one thing.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: ...Yes. The Abyssal power within you has stabilized again, and those strange symptoms you were experiencing seem to have completely disappeared.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Thank goodness!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We did it!

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: Hm, I wonder what it means though... Aside from the principles of alchemy, what other "law" of this world governs his being?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Look, it all turned out fine, so just leave it at that. Now that this one's out of danger, it's time for me to get out of here.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: You're leaving so soon? Don't humans usually throw a party after something like this?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: A party? Do I look like that kinda guy?

response.speaker: Wanderer
response.text: Anyway, come find me again next time you're in trouble. That's what "friends" are for, right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Some people never change...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: In a way, though, he is right. This is Durin's moment to celebrate, not the time for academic discussions.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Hey, I don't blame you for asking — and honestly, I'd be perfectly happy to talk about it. It's just... I wouldn't even know where to start.

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: It's alright, I'm sure we'll get a chance at some point. After all, your story's only just begun.

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: Mm-hmm...

response.speaker: Albedo
response.text: #Alright then... {NICKNAME} and Paimon, we'll part ways here. Given the extraordinary nature of the things we witnessed today, I need to make sure it's all recorded properly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, see ya!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, it's party time next— ...Huh!?
Dodoco— Dodoco—

response.speaker: Alice
response.text: Congratulations on completing your mission! Now then, as per our agreement, it's about time you returned that book.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She must've known the moment we finished... just like she said she would!

choices.text: It looks a lot more... free.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Ah, my writer and witness. It's been quite the journey, hasn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #You had special plans for {NICKNAME} from the start, didn't you...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Hahaha! But of course, that goes without saying! For a story to live on, it needs both a writer and a reader. Only then can my magic take effect.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: #I chose {NICKNAME} as the witness because of the special nature of who {M#he}{F#she} is.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: It's not easy finding someone with that kind of background, you know. For a moment, I even considered taking the role myself, hahaha.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Well, you were the only one who understood what was going on...

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: At least it made for an interesting story, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? What are you doing here, Tone-Deaf Bard?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: With the Hexenzirkel carrying out such a risky "experiment" in Mondstadt, it didn't cross your minds that the Anemo Archon might be slightly curious?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Sorry for the trouble, Lord Barbatos...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Think nothing of it — I daresay the Anemo Archon quite enjoyed coming along for the ride. Now then, as agreed, let us see the fruits of your labor.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Here, please take a look.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Well, well, well... Somehow, despite all my careful planning, it still turned out to be full of surprises.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: It never even crossed my mind that Rhinedottir's child would be capable of handling that kind of alchemy in her stead. When he asked for help with the materials, oh my, I nearly couldn't believe it!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: If only the others were here too... We could all celebrate together.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: I'm right here, you know. The only one who hasn't responded is the one busy stuffing her face over there.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Hahaha, is that you, Barbie? A little late to the party, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Come here, child. Let me take a closer look at you.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...Alright, Aunt Seer-Witch. Here I am.

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Just as I thought... This child's fate does not appear among the stars. Anya has accomplished what almost no one before her could.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: ...What does that mean?

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: Child, all you need to know is that you're very lucky indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So... What does it mean?

dialogues.speaker: Barbeloth
dialogues.text: (The teacup falls silent. Perhaps the mage's thoughts have already drifted elsewhere.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just like how she was in the story, huh...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Tell me, little Durin, what will you do next? I, for one, cannot wait to see how your story unfolds.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Well, there's so much I want to do... I'm not even sure where to begin!

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: How about settling your most recent regret?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not so fast, Tone-Deaf Bard... What exactly did you just tell Durin to do?

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: To make a long-overdue wish come true.

dialogues.speaker: "M"
dialogues.text: Thank you once again, Alice.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: ...How much time do you have left?

dialogues.speaker: "M"
dialogues.text: I believe... these should be my final moments. Just enough time to say goodbye to my dearest friend.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: This feels like having to say our final goodbyes all over again. I don't like it. Not one bit.

dialogues.speaker: "M"
dialogues.text: ...I don't know how to respond to that.

dialogues.speaker: "M"
dialogues.text: Strange, you were always such a cheerful figure in "my" stories... I even dubbed you the "merry-witch," you know...

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Oh, please... You know full well, it was your stories that first taught me what true pain and sadness felt like.

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Aside from saying goodbye to me, shouldn't you also leave a few words for the child?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Since the book will be his to continue, why don't you write him a little parting note?

dialogues.speaker: "M"
dialogues.text: There's no need. His mother already did that, long, long ago.

dialogues.speaker: "M"
dialogues.text: All that remains is for me to convey it on her behalf.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If we go this way, we'll be returning to the castle.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Returning to the castle...

choices.text: There's nothing challenging for you back there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! You'll just be hiding from your problems and pretending like none of this ever happened. Is that really what you want, Durin?

response.speaker: Durin
response.text: ...I see.

choices.text: You'll end up stuck in one place.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Do you think we could just... destroy it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why would you want to do that?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Be it the calamity headed for Mondstadt or my inability to leave behind a story of my own, doesn't it all come down to the fact that this heart never truly died?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: What if, here in this story, we could finally destroy it?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Hmm... Could Aunt Alice's magic really allow us to do what's theoretically meant to be impossible?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Either way, it's an intriguing idea. I'm not opposed to giving it a shot.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Durin...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: It's just...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: *sigh*... I'm still afraid, some day, even you guys will end up forgetting me. If there's even the slightest chance it'll prevent that, I'm willing to try anything.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: But I'm not sure if I can destroy it on my own. Chances are, I'm gonna need your help again.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: So please, everyone — help me destroy this heart, once and for all!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Not enough ink? Seriously...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Guess we need to turn to our other options.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's take another look around first.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Whatever happens next, Durin is going to need all of our help. Is everyone ready?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: So please, everyone — help me destroy this heart, once and for all!

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: There you go, your very own copy of the book. We wouldn't want one of the story's key witnesses to leave empty-handed now, would we?

dialogues.speaker: Alice
dialogues.text: Of course, this copy isn't "magical" in the same way — but rest assured, all the twists and turns are still there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We're ready.

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: "And so they flew together, Durin and Dvalin, over the skies of Mondstadt..."

dialogues.speaker: Venti
dialogues.text: Who'd have thought such words could ever have described a happy ending, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Durin and I need to check out a few other spots.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Durin and I need to check out a few other spots.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Unless the little dragon kept moving, eventually, he would be forgotten.

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Ahead of them was a storyless void, and they could go no further.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Sometimes, I wish I could just go back and see it again...

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Would he dare to hold this power back, or would he simply... give in?

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I can't feel a... a connection...

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You're not alone in this world, Durin. At the very least... you have me.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: I can't remember... anything... Who am I?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Your name is Durin, and there are many who still remember it.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: My name is Durin...

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: Wait! Where am I meant to go? What am I supposed to do?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Go make your wish come true, Durin.

dialogues.speaker: Durin
dialogues.text: My... wish?

dialogues.speaker: Narrator
dialogues.text: Facing that invisible wall... it was as if the little dragon... was staring at the uncrossable edge of existence itself...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: First, fetch the stickiest clay, and let it bind the scar of the break.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: Your story's not over yet!

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: I would like you to send this pen of mine into the future.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: You turn the page so the next chapter can begin.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: But his story... is far from over.

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The story will eventually reach its conclusion...

dialogues.speaker: <UNKNOWN>
dialogues.text: The prophecy is destined to come true...
